derivation_notes: Real ducts have viscous wall friction (Fanno-type dissipation) that generates entropy along the passage, shifting the effective area–Mach relation; the accumulated friction scales with duct length, here proxied by log(Ar) relative to the throat, and with dynamic-pressure-like M**2 modulated by the stagnation-temperature factor.
change_summary: Added a wall-friction dissipation correction term proportional to Cf that couples area ratio and Mach number, so the isentropic area–Mach relation is now perturbed by frictional entropy generation along the duct.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: Viscous wall friction dissipates flow energy and generates entropy along the duct, an effect jointly set by how far the flow has expanded (area ratio, proxied by log(Ar)) and by the local dynamic momentum (M**2), so the two already-present quantities combine to shift the area–Mach balance away from the ideal isentropic result.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: As Cf -> 0 (frictionless smooth wall or vanishingly short duct), the added term drops out and the equation collapses exactly to the isentropic area–Mach relation of the parent.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: For a given area ratio the measured subsonic Mach number is systematically lower than the isentropic prediction, with the discrepancy growing progressively larger as Ar increases downstream (log(Ar) growth) and at higher local speeds, rather than matching the ideal curve everywhere.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: Heat exchange through the duct walls (diabatic Rayleigh flow) alters the stagnation enthalpy, so the local Mach ratio depends jointly on the heat-addition rate and the compressibility factor of the gas, pushing the flow toward thermal choking as it accelerates.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: As Qh -> 0 the duct is adiabatic and the heat-exchange correction vanishes, recovering the original friction-plus-area implicit relation exactly.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The diabatic heat-exchange coefficient is a single fixed constant Qh independent of the imposed wall thermal state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Convective wall heat flux is proportional to the wall-to-gas temperature difference (Newton's law of cooling), so the Rayleigh-type heat-addition strength must vary with the externally set wall temperature Tw relative to reservoir temperature T0.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At Tw = T0 the temperature ratio term vanishes so the effective coefficient reduces to Qh0, and identifying Qh0 with the parent Qh recovers the original equation exactly.

change_summary: Added a threshold-activated separation blockage term whose contribution switches on via tanh only when the back-pressure-driven adverse gradient exceeds a Mach-dependent threshold, capturing diffuser stall not represented by the smooth friction/heat/boundary-layer terms.
